findings.claim: Original retail class-1 update callback 00463800 runs original lifecycle 00465370 and control 0043A3C0, which directly invokes original integrator 0043BDF0 (retail E8 at 0043A481) with the root object+0x18 matrix as an output. The active-vehicle path is distinct from an inactive fixedstep wheel-contact path.
findings.limitations: Observed in Ghidra original-instruction emulation with artificial camera-distance relevance gate, synthetic frame delta, emulated Win32/resource/math services; not continuous retail scheduler.

findings.claim: For both original-constructed, original-registered selected stock GTSi and bus under a controlled drive input and dt=1/60, two explicit class-1 update/camera callback pairs execute in the same emulator state. Original integrator changes root world Z from 0 to 0.0033333336468786 then 0.005625023506581783 and default camera returns with zero nonfinite original 00437F90 matrix words and zero nonfinite values in the six tested camera doubles on both frames.
findings.limitations: Values are controlled Ghidra-emulated numerical results, not validated retail world units or physically accurate in-game camera poses. The original 0049D400 and 004BA090 math boundaries are substituted.

findings.claim: Two separately executed selected-bus retail-x86 emulations of the controlled two-frame path produce byte-identical trace hashes; a separate idle input control completes two class callback/camera pairs without observed root translation.
findings.limitations: Both replay tests share deterministic emulation, identical synthetic inputs and mathematical substitutes; reproducibility does not establish hardware numerical parity.

findings.claim: The tested vehicle direction norm-squared measures about 0.472666 and 0.754794 after frames one and two. Original complete game-frame scheduling, positive fixed-step wheel-contact physics via 00438FD0, hardware x87 parity and normalized real-world pose remain unresolved.
findings.limitations: Do not interpret finite camera or moving pose as orthonormal rotation, true physics simulation or functioning original rasterization.
